memory_candidates.content: When a generated citation/freshness manifest exists for one repository's own declarations but a *consuming* repository's document cites those same declarations by line number, the manifest's seed list can be extended to cover the consuming document's citations too -- this closes the cross-repository half of the gate cheaply (no new script, no cross-repo write) as long as the consuming document's corrections are recorded name-keyed, resolved-against-the-manifest, and never as a fresh file:line, on this side for the consuming maintainers to apply by mechanical lookup.

To classify whether an old line-numbered citation is wrong-declaration versus correct-but-loose against a live tree, resolve the citation's target name through the generated manifest/exporter (never by eyeballing), then check whether the OLD cited line falls inside the CURRENT declaration's span (loose) or inside a neighbouring declaration's span (wrong). A uniform per-file line offset across an entire citation cluster is a strong signal of a single docstring-insertion commit -- confirm it with `git show <commit>` rather than asserting the cause.
